summary: P0: Sustained 5xx errors and streaming disconnects for AtlasPay during EU peak; major customer escalation
description: Issue summary: Between ~13:30 and 14:20 UTC on 2025-02-18 AtlasPay observed elevated 5xx rates (primarily 502/524) and sudden streaming disconnects during their EU afternoon peak. Several high-value payment flows degraded and a customer SRE escalated to support at 13:37 UTC. Impact: real-time payment validations failing (~35% error rate for affected routes), increased latency, and retries causing billing anomalies for the customer. Immediate business impact for AtlasPay production traffic in eu-west.
impact: Customer-facing payment verification calls experienced 30-40% error rates and intermittent truncated streaming responses for 15-20 minutes. Multiple failed transactions required manual retries; customer flagged potential SLA breach. Broad traffic from AtlasPay (multi-tenant enterprise account) hit the hosted API and routed to dedicated inference pool with mixed model pinning.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) From eu-west with AtlasPay API key simulate sustained tokenized payment validation workload using gpt-open-14b-v2 at 50 RPS and 512 token context over 15+ seconds streams.
2) Observe streaming proxy logs for connection resets and 5xx responses.
3) Trigger fallback routing to alternative model variants and watch increased failures when autoscaler reacts slowly.
logs_snippets:
2025-02-18T13:34:12Z streaming-proxy ERROR connection reset by peer (alloc: 1.2GB)
2025-02-18T13:35:07Z serving-runtime ERROR OOM while allocating KV cache for model gpt-open-14b-v2 (shard 3)
2025-02-18T13:36:41Z api-gateway WARN upstream 502 from serving-runtime
Request trace: trace_id=trc-0a9f-...; customer=AtlasPay; model=gpt-open-14b-v2
investigation_notes: Timeline reconstruction: At ~13:25 UTC there's a sudden 2.5x traffic spike from AtlasPay correlated with a scheduled marketing event. The dedicated pool autoscaler did not spin up capacity quickly enough due to a recent regression in the scale-up cooldown (linked INT-1102). Elevated memory pressure exposed a memory leak in streaming-proxy that manifested as connection resets and propagating 5xx from the serving runtime when KV cache allocations failed. Root cause: combination of increased sustained load + autoscaler cooldown regression + streaming-proxy memory leak in PR #12312 (later reverted). Evidence: heap growth in streaming-proxy, repeated OOM logs in serving-runtime shards, autoscaler logs showing suppressed scale-up within cooldown window.
resolution_summary: Short-term mitigation: 1) At 13:45 UTC support applied emergency routing policy to divert AtlasPay traffic to fallback model variant redwood-reranker-v1 and an alternate dedicated pool in eu-west-b. This reduced 5xxs and restored customer flow by 13:58 UTC. 2) SRE rolled back the streaming-proxy change (revert PR 12312) at 14:05 UTC which stopped heap growth. 3) Autoscaler cooldown param was temporarily reduced to allow faster scale-up (see INT-1102). Long-term fixes: fix memory leak in streaming-proxy (PR 12345), add KV cache soft-limits, and audit scale-up cooldown tests.
follow_up_actions:
1) Engineering to merge PR 12345 (streaming-proxy leak fix) and deploy to prod - target 2025-02-21.
2) Product infra to create a canary test for autoscaler cooldown during synthetic load - owner: Priya Rao - due 2025-03-01.
3) Add explicit per-customer circuit-breaker to prevent single customer from exhausting dedicated pool - owner: Platform - due 2025-03-10.
4) Postmortem on Confluence with quantitative impact and SLA reconciliation - owner: Maya Chen - due 2025-02-22.
customer_communications:
13:37 UTC: Acknowledged via support channel, opened P0 and set expectation of 30 min investigation.
13:50 UTC: Notified AtlasPay SRE that we were routing traffic to fallback pool and working on rollback; customer asked to pause a high-throughput job which they did at 13:52 UTC.
14:10 UTC: Confirmed mitigations were in place and asked for validation. 14:30 UTC: Final confirmation from AtlasPay that flows recovered to normal and they would wait for postmortem.
